title: Petrotectonics
description: Analysis of orogenic belts using petrography, thermochronology, and thermobarometry. Subject material changes each year.

title: Petrotectonics Laboratory
description: Analysis of orogenic belts using petrography, structural petrology, thermochronology, and thermobarometry.

title: Chemical Oceanography
description: An introduction to the chemistry of the oceans. Topics include composition and chemical equilibria of seawater, biogeochemical cycling, sediment chemistry, atmospheric exchange, circulation and rates of mixing based on chemical tracers, and the impact of ocean chemistry on climate change.

title: Climates of the Past
description: Introduction to climate and ocean history. Techniques used to reconstruct terrestrial, oceanic and atmospheric conditions. Evolution of climate over the last million years. Theories of climate change, including Milankovich hypothesis, greenhouse effect and internal feedback. Anthropogenic climate change.

title: Seminar in Geology-Presentation
description: Presentation of research topics to meeting of Earth 260.

title: Tracer and Contaminant Hydrology
description: Introduction to principles of chemical and isotope tracer hydrology. Emphasis on methods of groundwater dating, the use of tracers as management tools, and contaminate plume monitoring. Research paper required.

title: Computational Approaches for Geological and Biological Sciences
description: This course offers a comprehensive introduction to data analysis using Python and R. Students will not only learn the fundamentals of coding but also develop skills in basic statistical analysis, data visualization, data management, and machine learning. Lab sessions will be designed to reinforce the concepts learned through hands-on practice. No coding experience is required. For graduate students, the course places additional emphasis on applying computational techniques and relevant software to analyze biological data, particularly in genomics. Graduate students will also engage in the development of a final project of their choice.

title: Geological Oceanography
description: Morphology, formation, and evolution of ocean basins; crustal structure and composition of ocean margins; source and composition of marine sediments; marine sediment as repository of paleoclimate and paleo-ocean circulation records. Paleoceanographic changes in relation to tectonics and changes in orbital parameters, links between changes in ocean circulation and climate changes.

title: Ore Deposits and Mineral Resources
description: Distribution and characteristics of major classes of mineral deposits - their geologic framework, mineralogy, and structure. Lectures explore petrogenetic models for ore-formation. Laboratory exercises and field trips stress recognition of ore and accessory minerals, zoning, and exploration strategies. The field trip ranges from 1-4 days long

title: Seminar in Field Geology
description: Field trips of one day or more, organized as opportune. Appropriate report required for each trip.

title: Field Trips in Earth Science
description: Opportunity to see classic geological localities in the field. Locations vary depending on instructor(s). Lectures through the quarter cover background material needed to understand what is being observed/studied in the field. This material includes specified readings, homework assignments, exercises and exams. Lab work may also be required. Lecture, 3 hours; field, up to 6 weeks.

title: Field Studies in Marine Bio/Geochemistry
description: Studies in marine bio/geochemistry with the opportunity of going to sea or into the field on land. Lectures cover techniques of seafloor mapping using bottom photography, marine bio/geochemical sampling, and methods of data reduction and sample analysis. Labs include analysis of data/samples collected.Lecture, 3 hours; lab, up to 7 hours; field, up to 6 weeks.
